A long weekend is defined as a holiday that falls on a Friday or Monday, or a holiday that falls on a weekend but is observed on the nearest weekday, giving you three consecutive days off.

|------|---------|-------------|---------------------------|--------------|
| **Jan 1** | New Year’s Day | Sunday | Observed Mon Jan 2 | **Jan 1–3** (Sun–Mon) |

| **Mar 10** | Good Friday | Friday | — | **Mar 10–12** (Fri–Sun) |
| **May 22** | Victoria Day | Monday | — | **May 20–22** (Sat–Mon) |
| **Jul 1** | Canada Day | Saturday | Observed Fri Dec 31? (No, observed on Sat) | **Jul 1–2** (Sat–Sun) |
| **Aug 7** | Civic Holiday (BC, NB, NL, PEI, SK, ON, YT) | Monday | — | **Aug 5–7** (Sat–Mon) |
| **Sep 4** | Labour Day | Monday | — | **Sep 2–4** (Sat–Mon) |
| **Oct 9** | Thanksgiving | Monday | — | **Oct 7–9** (Sat–Mon) |
| **Nov 11** | Remembrance Day | Monday | — | **Nov 9–11** (Sat–Mon) |
| **Dec 25** | Christmas Day | Monday | — | **Dec 23–25** (Sat–Mon) |
| **Dec 26** | Boxing Day | Tuesday | — | **Dec 24–26** (Sat–Tue) |

### Notes

* **Family Day** is observed in several provinces (AB, BC, NB, NL, PEI, SK, ON, YT). It is *not* observed in Quebec, the Northwest Territories, Nunavut, or the remaining provinces.
* **Civic Holiday** is observed in many provinces on the first Monday of August, but not in all. In provinces where it isn’t observed, the long weekend will not exist.
* **New Year’s Day** falls on a Sunday in 2023, so the observed day is Monday, Jan 2. The long weekend spans Sun Jan 1–Mon Jan 2.
* **Christmas Day** falls on a Monday, so the long weekend spans Sat Dec 23–Mon Dec 25.
* **Boxing Day** falls on a Tuesday, giving a long weekend from Sat Dec 24–Tue Dec 26.

Feel free to adjust the list based on your specific province or territory if you’re planning a trip or scheduling time off!
